tagline: AI payment routing for mid-market e-commerce

materials.name: SynthPay Series A Deck.txt
materials.text:
Slide 1 — Company: SynthPay
AI-powered payment routing that cuts processing costs and improves authorization rates for mid-market e-commerce retailers.

Slide 2 — The Problem: Mid-market e-commerce companies lose 1.5–2.5% of revenue to suboptimal payment routing — wrong processor selection, avoidable declines, excessive interchange fees. Legacy payment processors offer static routing with no real-time optimization. This affects $180B in annual transaction volume.

Slide 3 — The Solution: SynthPay's ML engine routes each transaction in real-time across multiple acquiring banks and payment processors, selecting the optimal path based on card type, merchant category, issuer history, and fraud score. We improve authorization rates by an average of 3.2 percentage points and reduce blended processing fees by 1.8% across our customer base.

Slide 4 — Market: The payment orchestration and routing software market is a $4.2B annual opportunity growing at 22% per year. Mid-market e-commerce (GMV $10M–$500M) represents the underserved segment — too large for Stripe Billing defaults, too small for enterprise treasury teams. We are the only AI-native routing layer purpose-built for this segment with no direct competitors.

Slide 5 — Traction: ARR grew from $620,000 in Q1 2024 to $2.1M in Q4 2024. We have 31 active merchants. Net revenue retention is 138%. Average contract value is $68,000 annually. Logo churn has been zero since launch.

Slide 6 — Unit Economics: Gross margin is 74% on a fully-loaded COGS basis. LTV/CAC ratio is 7.2x. Payback period is 11 months. CAC is $9,400.

Slide 7 — Fundraising: We are raising $12M Series A at a $58M pre-money valuation. Existing investors include Quiet Capital and two angels from the Stripe founding team. The round is 60% committed.

Slide 8 — Team: CEO Winston Osei previously ran product and growth at Brex (joined pre-Series B, left post-IPO filing). CTO Lena Park was a founding engineer at Plaid's payments infrastructure team. VP Sales Darius Mehta has 8 years of enterprise SaaS sales including 4 years at Adyen.

Slide 9 — Compliance: SynthPay is PCI DSS Level 1 compliant. We hold no cardholder data and operate as a payment facilitator, not a money transmitter, which limits our regulatory surface area. No legal disputes, no regulatory investigations.

Slide 10 — Roadmap: Cross-border routing launching Q2 2025. Embedded finance partnerships with Shopify and WooCommerce plugins in beta.

materials.name: Founder Call Transcript.txt
materials.text:
Investor: Walk me through the revenue and retention numbers in detail.

Winston: Sure. We ended Q4 2024 at $2.1M ARR. That's up from $620K at the start of the year, so roughly 3.4x growth in twelve months. We have 31 active merchants and three more in the final implementation stage. NRR has been 138% on a dollar-weighted basis — expansion comes primarily from merchants adding additional Shopify storefronts or launching new geographies. Logo churn has been zero.

Investor: What's driving the authorization improvement claim?

Winston: We track pre- and post-SynthPay authorization rates at the card-by-card level for each merchant. On average across the installed base, we see a 3.2 percentage point improvement. The range is 1.8 to 5.4 depending on the merchant's legacy routing setup. We can share merchant-level data under NDA.

Investor: Who do you see as direct competitors?

Winston: In our segment, we don't see direct AI-native competitors. Spreedly is orchestration middleware but doesn't do ML optimization. Primer.io has routing but it's rule-based, not ML. Stripe Optimized Checkout is closed-loop and doesn't work cross-processor. We see legacy orchestration tools but nothing purpose-built for mid-market with AI-native routing.

Investor: Tell me about the fundraising terms.

Winston: $12M Series A, $58M pre-money. We've got a $10M lead commitment from Northzone pending final diligence. Two existing angels converting their notes. That's about 60% of the round. We'd like to close in 8 weeks.

Investor: Team background?

Winston: I ran product at Brex from Series C through the IPO filing process. Lena was one of the first five engineers on Plaid's payments core. Darius spent four years at Adyen running mid-market enterprise sales in North America.

materials.name: Competitive Landscape Notes.txt
materials.text:
SynthPay Internal Competitive Analysis — November 2024

Payment Orchestration and Routing Market

Direct and adjacent competitors:

1. Spreedly — Payment orchestration middleware for multi-processor setups. Not ML-optimized but widely adopted. Used by mid-market e-commerce as a gateway abstraction layer. Competes on integrations breadth. ARR publicly disclosed at $35M (2023 press).

2. Primer.io — Rule-based payment routing with a visual workflow builder. Strong in Europe. Raised $50M Series B in 2022. Does not use ML for routing decisions; relies on merchant-defined rules. Direct feature overlap with SynthPay in routing logic, diverges in ML vs. rules approach.

3. Stripe Optimized Checkout (Adaptive Acceptance) — Stripe's internal ML-based authorization optimization for Stripe-acquiring merchants. Closed ecosystem, not cross-processor. Significant for Stripe-only merchants.

4. Checkout.com Smart Routing — ML routing within Checkout.com's acquiring network. Not cross-processor. Competes for merchants who route exclusively through Checkout.

5. Basis Theory / Very Good Security (VGS) — Focus on cardholder data vaulting with some routing capabilities. Adjacent, not direct.

6. Gr4vy — Payment orchestration with routing. Early stage (Series A, 2022). Direct competitor in orchestration, limited ML capability.

Key takeaway: SynthPay's claim of no direct AI-native competitor is partially accurate — no competitor combines cross-processor routing with ML-optimization at the mid-market price point. However, Spreedly, Primer.io, and Gr4vy are real alternatives that customers evaluate. The 'no direct competitors' framing overstates the competitive moat.
